messages:
incident_bot: Pagerduty P0: sudden increase in cross-region 5xxs and tail latency for eu-central-1 -> us-west-2 traffic. Rule: cost-steer-with-fallback. Trigger: 5xx rate > 8% and p99 latency > 900ms. Escalating to #incidents. :rotating_light:
rita_sre: acked. Oncall pages in progress (tom_neteng). Collecting quick impact: is this customer-visible?
priya_support: yes — several enterprise customers in EU reported errors and elevated latencies. I've flagged top-5 customers and opened tickets. Marking impact: partial degraded for eu origins.
tom_neteng: I'm on it. Looking at routing decisions for eu->us-west flows. Initial trace shows an uptick in DNS resolution flaps for eu backend endpoints in eu-central-1. Our routing policy considers endpoint health + dns_ttl_age; if DNS TTL expired we fallback to cost preference.
josh_infra: cloud provider reported a control-plane networking event affecting eu-central-1c; many instances returned stale DNS answers for ~4m per their report.
lina_ops: running a query against route_decisions: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM decisions WHERE src='eu-central-1' AND chosen_region!='eu-central-1' AND ts > now() - interval '15 minutes'` -> results show a 7x spike.
tom_neteng: that aligns. The policy we rolled last week (cost-favoring tie-break) will choose us-west-2 when health metadata is missing. With DNS flaps, endpoints look unhealthy -> traffic spills. Need emergency mitigation: temporary pin or increase DNS TTL tolerance.
rita_sre: For quick mitigation, we have two options: 1) push a control-plane override to pin src eu-central-1 to eu endpoints (priority 110), or 2) disable the cost-favor tie-break flag globally. Which is lower risk?
josh_infra: override route is quick, lowest blast radius. I'll prepare override and apply to eu prefixes now.
priya_support: I'll notify all affected customers with a short message: "We've applied a temporary routing pin to keep you in-region while we investigate DNS flaps. Expect normal performance to resume shortly"
deploy_bot: ACTION: override-route create requested by josh_infra. command: `redwoodctl routes create --scope eu-central-1 --priority 110 --target-region eu-central-1 --reason "emergency pin due to DNS flap"`
incident_bot: ACTION LOG: override-route id=ovr-1976 created at 1976550012 by josh_infra.
tom_neteng: verifying metrics... cross-region egress from eu-central-1 to us-west-2 dropped ~92% in 40s, eu-origin 5xx down to baseline. Good.
lina_ops: adding short-lived alert to watch for override churn and provider recovery: `alert.override_spike_eu` 1m window.
rita_sre: while override is holding, let's root cause — is this purely provider DNS flaps or our DNS caching logic amplified?
josh_infra: looks like caching. We recently reduced DNS cache TTL tolerance to prioritize freshness; that makes us more sensitive to provider flaps. Combined with cost-tie-break change -> amplification.
omitted_bot: (system) Note: don't use omitted_bot in participants list — just a placeholder.
tom_neteng: proposed next steps: 1) revert tie-break flag to safe (prefer-local-if-metadata-missing) on canary control-plane slice; 2) keep override in place until canary is validated; 3) add synthetic probe to catch DNS-flap-triggered routing flips. Lina, can you run the canary?
lina_ops: starting canary rollback for policy v2.8.3 -> v2.8.2 on 10% control-plane edge nodes. command: `policyctl promote --from v2.8.3 --to v2.8.2 --canary 10`
deploy_bot: CANARY: started at 1976550120 by lina_ops. Monitor window: 60s.
tom_neteng: monitoring shows no regression in EU-origin errors during canary. Rolling canary to 50% now.
josh_infra: preparing to remove override once control-plane promotes. I'll stand by to remove at tl;dr: await signal.
priya_support: customers updated in thread and status page. No SLA credits yet but logging usage impact for review.
incident_bot: CANARY PASS: control-plane rollback promotion completed at 1976550250.
josh_infra: removing emergency override now: `redwoodctl routes delete ovr-1976`
incident_bot: ACTION LOG: override-route id=ovr-1976 deleted at 1976550285 by josh_infra.
tom_neteng: post-change metrics: cross-region egress normalized, eu-origin p99 latency back to baseline, 5xxs resolved. Priya, confirm customer reports.
priya_support: customers reporting success, closing individual tickets. Status page updated to reflect mitigation and ongoing postmortem.
rita_sre: assigning follow-ups: 1) add test coverage for DNS TTL tolerance + tie-break interactions (owner: tom_neteng), 2) add synthetic to detect provider DNS flaps and auto-apply temporary pin (owner: josh_infra), 3) review recent policy rollout process (owner: lina_ops).
lina_ops: creating tasks in INF-8401, INF-8402, INF-8403 with 7d SLAs.
pagerduty: Reminder: scheduled on-call handoff in 30m from tom_neteng -> rita_sre.
rita_sre: I'll take follow-up. Drafting customer-impact summary: estimated affected requests ~2.4k, peak affected users ~18 orgs, incident duration ~12 minutes from detection to final rollback/remove override.
incident_bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: emergency override + policy rollback mitigated the issue. Root cause: combination of provider DNS flaps in eu-central-1c + recent policy tie-break that preferred lower-cost region when health metadata missing, amplified by reduced DNS cache tolerance. Postmortem invite posted to #postmortems at 1976550400.
tom_neteng: leaving handoff notes in runbook: commands run, override id, canary steps, monitoring queries. Available for async questions.
priya_support: billing ops notified for potential credits.
rita_sre: thanks all. I'll own the write-up and coordinate with eng and support for customer messaging. Closing thread after postmortem kickoff. :white_check_mark:
